subtitle: Five candidate workflows where Claude can save time, capacity, or risk inside Hallboys' current systems

slides.title: Claude at Hallboys — Operational Workflows
slides.subtitle: Five candidate workflows where Claude can save time, capacity, or risk inside Hallboys' current systems

slides.title: Hallboys Context
slides.subtitle: What we are designing for, in your environment
points: GC operating with Acumatica as ERP and system of record
3-person internal IT team — no spare capacity for a 6-month build
One AP clerk processing every invoice end-to-end
Claude already in active use across the organization, mostly ad-hoc
No deployed agentic workflows today, no shared skill library, no audit trail
Field, office, and finance work happen on different cadences (daily, weekly, monthly)

slides.title: Current State — How work happens today
left_points: Estimator manually compares sub quotes in Excel — 3 to 5 vendors per package
AP clerk receives invoices via email, posts each one in Acumatica AP screen
PMs assemble closeout packages from shared drives, no formal pre-check
Schedule changes flow through verbal updates and Acumatica project records
right_points: Equipment scheduled by hand against a master schedule — no conflict checker
Sub coordination happens in weekly meetings and ad-hoc texts
Job folders live partly on Acumatica, partly on shared drives
Closeout punch and warranty docs collected late, often during retainage chase

slides.title: Problem Framing — Where time and money leak
left_points: Estimator hours absorbed by quote comparison instead of scoping new work
AP clerk capacity capped — invoice volume grows faster than headcount
Retainage held longer than necessary because closeout packages are incomplete
Idle crew days from schedule conflicts that were preventable
right_points: Sub scope gaps surfacing after award, not before
Duplicate invoices and pricing drift not caught consistently
Closeout missing items found by owner, not by Hallboys, costing trust
Claude usage today is private to each user — no reuse, no review

slides.title: Five candidate workflows
slides.body: Each is bounded to one role, one cadence, and one measurable outcome. None require new systems.

slides.title: Use Case 1 — Subcontractor quote comparison
points: Current workflow: estimator opens 3-5 sub quote PDFs, builds an Excel comparison by hand, ~4 hrs per package
Intervention: estimator drops quotes into a Claude skill that returns scope deltas, missing line items, and risk flags
Tomorrow morning change: estimator opens a pre-built comparison instead of building one — picks the winner
Measurable impact: ~3 hrs saved per multi-vendor bid package; estimator capacity for additional packages per week
Confidence: medium (estimate, validate week 1 against last quarter's bid log)
Risks / limitations: missed scope nuance on unusual trades; estimator must still spot-check; Not available — current bid-package volume per estimator

slides.title: Use Case 2 — Equipment and crew scheduling coordination
points: Current workflow: scheduler reconciles equipment list, sub commitments, and master schedule manually each week
Intervention: weekly schedule + equipment list go into a Claude skill that surfaces overlaps, missing deliveries, and dependency breaks
Tomorrow morning change: Monday schedule meeting opens with a pre-flagged conflict list — scheduler decides each call
Measurable impact: avoiding 1 idle crew day per quarter on a mid-size job is ~$5K-8K — scheduler still owns approvals
Confidence: low-medium (depends on Hallboys' historical conflict rate, which we have not yet measured)
Risks / limitations: schedule data quality in Acumatica drives output quality; Not available — historical idle-day cost

slides.title: Use Case 3 — AP exception triage (assisted only)
points: Current workflow: AP clerk opens each invoice email, manually keys into Acumatica AP screen, checks PO, posts
Intervention: Claude pre-reads each invoice — extracts vendor/amount/PO match, flags duplicates and pricing anomalies — clerk still posts
Tomorrow morning change: clerk works from a triaged queue with anomalies surfaced first — no new screen, beside Acumatica
Measurable impact: target 1.5x to 1.8x current invoice volume reviewed per day at same catch rate
Confidence: medium (target validated through 30-day shadow mode before any clerk workflow change)
Risks / limitations: Claude never writes to Acumatica; missed anomalies still possible; Not available — current duplicate-invoice rate

slides.title: Use Case 4 — Project closeout document checks
points: Current workflow: PM assembles closeout package manually, often late in the project; gaps caught by owner, not Hallboys
Intervention: PM uploads closeout folder to Claude skill that checks against the Hallboys closeout SOP — missing items, mismatched dates, lien gaps
Tomorrow morning change: PM gets a missing-item list before sending the package, fixes gaps in-house
Measurable impact: avoiding 1 retainage delay per quarter is the breakeven for this workflow alone
Confidence: medium-high (depends on a documented Hallboys closeout SOP — confirm exists)
Risks / limitations: SOP must be current; Not available — average retainage tied up per delayed closeout

slides.title: Use Case 5 — Claude skill governance
points: Current workflow: every Claude user writes their own prompts; no version control, no audit, no reuse
Intervention: small set of versioned skills (one per workflow above) owned by IT, used by everyone in the shared workspace
Tomorrow morning change: estimators, PMs, and AP open Claude to find the right skill already published, not blank prompts
Measurable impact: reduce duplicate prompt rebuilding; consistent outputs; new hires productive day one
Confidence: high (mechanical change — depends only on IT publishing the skills)
Risks / limitations: skills decay if no one maintains; requires named owner; Not available — current Claude user count and hours/week per user

slides.title: Day-to-Day Workflow Changes — who does what differently
rows: Builds bid comparison in Excel, ~4 hrs/package
Reconciles schedule by hand each Monday
Opens Monday meeting with conflict list in hand
Opens each invoice cold, posts to Acumatica
Works from triaged queue, posts to Acumatica as today
Assembles package, gaps found by owner
Pre-checks against SOP, fixes gaps before sending
Owns 5 published skills, monthly review cadence

slides.title: Quantified Impact — what we measure in the pilot
rows: All 5 skills in active use by day 60

slides.title: Failure Modes — what breaks, where the human stays involved
left_points: Misses scope nuance on unusual trades in quote comparison
Surfaces a false-positive schedule conflict when Acumatica data is stale
Flags a legitimate invoice as a duplicate (similar vendor, similar amount)
Misses a closeout doc not covered by the SOP
Skill output drifts as vendors or scope conventions change
slides.right_header: Where the human owns the call
right_points: Estimator picks the bid winner — Claude cannot
Scheduler approves every change — Claude only flags
AP clerk posts every invoice in Acumatica — Claude never writes
PM signs every closeout package — Claude only lists gaps
IT lead approves every skill version, monthly review cadence

slides.title: Why this fits Hallboys
left_points: Acumatica stays the system of record — no replacement, no integration risk
AP clerk role unchanged — capacity expands, headcount does not shrink
3-person IT team can own this — skills are configured, not engineered
Builds on Claude usage you already have — no new vendor relationship
Pilots fit inside existing meeting cadences — no new ceremonies
right_points: No custom system build, no new ERP
No data leaves the Hallboys Claude workspace
No black-box automation on AP, contracts, or schedule
No 6-month rollout — 60-day pilot with day-30 kill points
No vendor lock-in — skills handed to IT at end of pilot

slides.title: Pilot Plan — 60 days, exit any time
slides.subtitle: Two workflows in active use, three queued behind them
points: Days 1-7: pull baselines — last quarter's bid log, current closeout SOP, AP volume
Days 8-21: build and publish 2 skills (recommend quote comparison + closeout) in shared workspace
Days 22-30: pilot in production with one estimator and one PM; day-30 kill points enforced
Days 31-45: continue if signals clear; pull AP duplicate-rate baseline; consider adding AP triage
Days 46-60: hand skills to IT for ongoing ownership; deliver weekly scorecard to Sarat throughout
Exit at any review point with no penalty; all skills and data stay with Hallboys

slides.title: Next step — agree on two workflows for the 60-day pilot
slides.body: Recommend quote comparison + closeout. Both have clean baselines. Both leave Acumatica untouched. Decide from data.
